units.text: INT. HUSBAND - CONTINUOUS
What does this mean, sir? You don’t mean to say that this charming, clever young lady has been so foolish as to accept you?
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: Certainly, father! And Chiltern’s been wise enough to accept the seat in the Cabinet.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: I am very glad to hear that, Chiltern . . . I congratulate you, sir. If the country doesn’t go to the dogs or the Radicals, we shall have you Prime Minister, some day.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: Enter MASON.
Luncheon is on the table, my Lady!
units.name: MASON

units.text: MASON goes out .
You’ll stop to luncheon, Lord Caversham, won’t you?
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: With pleasure, and I’ll drive you down to Downing Street afterwards, Chiltern. You have a great future before you, a great future. Wish I could say the same for you, sir.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: To LORD GORING.
But your career will have to be entirely domestic.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: Yes, father, I prefer it domestic.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: And if you don’t make this young lady an ideal husband, I’ll cut you off with a shilling.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: An ideal husband! Oh, I don’t think I should like that. It sounds like something in the next world.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: What do you want him to be then, dear?
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: He can be what he chooses. All I want is to be . . . to be . . . oh! a real wife to him.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Upon my word, there is a good deal of common sense in that, Lady Chiltern.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: They all go out except SIR ROBERT CHILTERN.
He sinks in a chair , wrapt in thought .
After a little time LADY CHILTERN returns to look for him .
Leaning over the back of the chair .
Aren’t you coming in, Robert?
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Taking her hand .
Gertrude, is it love you feel for me, or is it pity merely?
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Kisses him .
It is love, Robert. Love, and only love. For both of us a new life is beginning.
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: THE NORTHUMBERLAND PRESS, NEWCASTLE-UPON-TYNE
